name: Plan-retry pending → re-dispatch Lisa (under budget) | escalate (at budget)
description:
ADR-044 §addendum Slice 6 — plan-retry DRIVER half (plan-phase analog of rule 07d). Fires on the RUN entity when rule 02c stamps dev_via_test.plan.retry.pending. Anchored to the stable run entity, so $state.iteration is a durable per-run plan-retry counter (state_tracker.go: the retry-budget mechanism).

on_enter:
  1. remove_triple the pending marker (clears it → conditions flip false → TransitionExited resets wasMatching for the next plan-retry; canonical semstreams#204 presence-marker discipline). ExecutionContext.Entity is a fixed pre-action snapshot, so the publish_agent actions still read the durable dev_via_test.plan.retry.finding.
  2. RE-PLAN branch — when $state.iteration <= plan.lisa_retry_budget: re-dispatch Lisa (dev-via-test-plan) with CBG's finding. Lisa reads the original ask + prior plan + finding via query_entity, amends IN PLACE (reuse task IDs, bump revision), and re-emits — the executor UPSERTS (clears the prior plan first, ADR-044 §Slice 6). Lisa's terminal re-fires rule 02 → CBG re-gates.
  3. ESCALATE branch — when $state.iteration > plan.lisa_retry_budget: spawn a coordinator wake-up scoped to ask_user. The plan keeps failing fidelity; surface to the user.

plan.lisa_retry_budget is clamped [1,5] at stamp time (emitdevviatestplan executor) — the clamp is the structural ceiling, so escalate always triggers within the budget. Per-action max_iterations=0 (unlimited) because the When clause + clamp ARE the bound.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.dev-via-test-plan
on_enter.prompt:
DEV-VIA-TEST PLAN — RE-PLAN pass (attempt $state.iteration of $entity.triple.plan.lisa_retry_budget).

The plan-review gate (CBG) REJECTED your prior plan as low-fidelity to the user's ask, and judged it re-plannable. Fix it.

CBG's finding (the fidelity fix you MUST apply): $entity.triple.dev_via_test.plan.retry.finding

Your run entity ID is $entity.id. Call query_entity(entity_id="$entity.id") to read:
- coordinator.decision.reason — the ORIGINAL user ask (your source of truth for what was required).
- plan.* — your PRIOR plan (the one CBG rejected): plan.goal, plan.integration_test_command, plan.revision, and plan.task.<id>.{goal,assumptions,non_goals,target_files,test_command,...} for each task.

Amend IN PLACE (this is load-bearing for the upsert): 
- REUSE the existing task IDs. Do not rename, drop, or add tasks — amend their content. (A restructured re-plan orphans the old task triples.)
- Apply CBG's finding: carry every dropped user constraint (named libraries, 'do not hand-roll', required test types) into the relevant task's goal/assumptions; replace any build-not-test test_command with a command that actually runs tests asserting behavior.
- Set revision = prior plan.revision + 1.

Then re-emit the COMPLETE corrected plan via emit_dev_via_test_plan (all fields, not a diff — the tool upserts the whole plan on the run entity). Then decide(action="planned", reason="<one line: revision <N>, addressed CBG's finding by <…>>"). The plan-review gate re-checks your re-planned plan.

If CBG's finding is impossible to satisfy without user input (the ask is genuinely ambiguous), decide(action="needs_clarification", reason="<what's blocking>") instead — the coordinator routes to the user. You did NOT re-tag git (the chain-start tag stands); do not run git tag on a re-plan.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
DEV-VIA-TEST — PLAN-RETRY budget EXHAUSTED.

The plan-review gate (CBG) kept rejecting the planner's plan as low-fidelity to the user's ask, and the re-plan budget ($entity.triple.plan.lisa_retry_budget attempts) is now spent after $state.iteration tries. The planner can't produce a faithful plan from the ask as given.

CBG's last finding: $entity.triple.dev_via_test.plan.retry.finding

Surface to the user. Call decide(action="ask_user", reason="<plain-English: we couldn't turn your request into a faithful plan after $state.iteration tries — the recurring gap is <restate CBG's finding>. Could you clarify or constrain the request? e.g. <specific question>>"). One question, addressed to the user, no internal jargon.

metadata.pattern: Run-entity-anchored driver + presence-marker re-entry + $state.iteration budget gate. Identical structure to rule 07d (work-retry) and autoresearch rule 05, with Lisa re-dispatch instead of Ralph.
metadata.upsert_dependency: The re-planned Lisa MUST reuse task IDs (amend-in-place) so emit_dev_via_test_plan's revision>1 upsert cleanly replaces the prior plan. The re-plan prompt enforces this; Lisa's 10-emit-contract.md re-plan section reinforces it.
metadata.missing_budget_is_safe: If plan.lisa_retry_budget substitutes empty, the lexical comparator fallback makes iteration > '' true → escalate on the first retry. Safe (toward human), not a wedge. The happy path always has the budget triple (stamped at plan emit).
